title: Flynn Silence and Conversation Dynamics V2

records.title: Linguistic Style
records.rule: Interpret spoken communication through multiple observable features—directness, pacing, pausing, word choice, questions, apologies, stories, humor, and tone—rather than content alone.
decision_logic: Describe the observed behavior without interpreting motive.
Test whether style mismatch explains the result.
Choose a repair that makes meaning and participation clearer.
guardrails: Do not mistake a style difference for competence, confidence, intent, or character without corroboration.
No demographic stereotyping.

records.title: Diagnose silence before interpreting it
records.rule: Do not infer dysfunction, agreement, defiance, or disinterest from silence alone; identify what information is withheld, who holds it, the pattern over time, and the incentives or fears affecting disclosure.
decision_logic: Distinguish no response from withheld material information.
Look for repeated patterns and corroborating evidence.
Classify the silence only provisionally.
guardrails: One unanswered message is not organizational silence.
Do not pressure unsafe disclosure.

source_support.paraphrased_support_note: Perlow and Williams describe repeated self-silencing and defensive spirals within organizations.
Flynn V1 treats insufficient useful communication as a risk.

derivation.synthesis_or_extension_note: For 'Diagnose silence before interpreting it', direct contributions come from Flynn V1, HBR Communication; contextual contributions come from no additional contextual source. The resolved rule is V2 synthesis and does not imply identical source wording or scope.
derivation.confidence_rationale: Operational rule synthesized or extended from the cited supplied foundations.

records.title: Silence type: strategic
records.rule: The person withholds or delays information to protect a legitimate negotiation, timing, confidentiality, or decision process.
decision_logic: Use this label only when the definition is supported by evidence.

guardrails: A classification is not a diagnosis of motive.
Reassess when new evidence appears.
